case_title: Shiva Kumar @ Shiva @ Shiv Amurthy v. State of Karnataka
accused_occupation: Driver (vehicle driver for the victim's employer's transport)
previous_criminal_record: No - first offence per Trial Court
evidence_type: Recovery (body and clothing recovered at accused's instance); other evidence types not described in this judgment
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal rape and murder of a young married woman who was taken in the accused's vehicle on the pretext of an unavailable company cab
mitigating_circumstances: Age 27 at conviction, wife, small child, aged parents, first offence (as noted by Trial Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.366, 376 and 302 IPC; life imprisonment (rigorous) for the rest of life for s.302
high_court_outcome: Dismissed accused's appeal against conviction and sentence and State's appeal for enhancement
offence_finally_established: IPC s.366 (kidnapping/abduction), s.376 (rape), s.302 (murder); only the sentence for s.302 was modified
neutral_facts: The victim, a married employee of a company with an office in Electronic City, Bengaluru, often worked late nights and was provided company transport by car on designated routes. At about 2:00 a.m., after leaving the office, the victim was told by the accused, who was the vehicle driver, that the usual vehicle on the victim's route was unavailable and that the victim would have to travel in the accused's vehicle on another route. The victim got into the car driven by the accused. The victim's maternal uncle later lodged a complaint that the victim was missing. Subsequently, the victim's dead body was recovered at the instance of the accused, and the clothes and footwear of the victim were found near the body. The prosecution case was that the victim was raped and then killed in a brutal manner, and the victim's life was cut short at the age of 28. The investigation thus rested on the recovery of the body and the victim's belongings following the accused's disclosure, together with the circumstances of the victim's last journey in the accused's vehicle.
offence_severity: Death penalty as the capital punishment (alternative life imprisonment under s.53 IPC 'secondly'); minimum not stated
physical_harm: Death of the victim following rape; other injuries not described
key_evidence_accepted: Recovery of the body at accused's instance and of clothing and footwear near the body; the court accepted that the prosecution established rape and s.366 offence
post_offence_conduct: Body recovered at the accused's instance; no other post-offence conduct discussed
custody_duration: Approximately 17 years 2 months (as submitted by appellant's counsel; not a court finding)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 31.05.2016; Supreme Court: 28.03.2023
legal_representation: Accused: K. Parameshwar, Shekhar G Devasa and others (M/s. Devasa & Co.). State: Shubhranshu Padhi, Vishal Banshal and others
investigation_status: Complaint lodged by victim's maternal uncle; body recovered at accused's instance; charge sheet and other steps not stated
procedural_irregularity: Trial Court wrongly directed that the accused not be released for the rest of his life; the court held it could not have made such an order
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and life imprisonment for rest of life. High Court: both appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: convictions upheld; s.302 sentence modified to life with release only after 30 years actual sentence
prosecution_argument: Constitutional Courts can impose modified sentences even where death penalty not imposed; the most stringent punishment was warranted on the facts; High Court rightly upheld life sentence for the entirety of life
defence_argument: Modified sentence only by Constitutional Courts and only when commuting death penalty; Sessions Court powerless; accused has young family, no antecedents, good jail conduct and has completed a B.A. in jail (as submitted)
legal_principle_applied: Constitutional Courts (High Court and Supreme Court) may impose a fixed-term life sentence of more than 14 years even without death penalty; no remission before the fixed period expires; sentence must not be below 14 years under s.433A Cr.P.C.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan (2016) 7 SCC 1 (followed); Swamy Shraddananda (2) (2008) 13 SCC 767 (referred); Sahib Hussain (2013) 9 SCC 778 and Gurvail Singh (2013) 10 SCC 631 (referred)
sentencing_rationale: Brutal crime shocks conscience; a fixed-term sentence was needed rather than a life term subject to remission; a thirty-year fixed term was held appropriate after weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances, victim's rights and public confidence
judicial_mitigating_factors: Age 27 at conviction, wife, small child, aged parents, first offence; possibility of reformation considered
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal nature of the crime; rape and murder of a woman; need to protect safety of women working at night; undue leniency would harm public confidence; rights of victim
other_sentence_order: Accused to undergo life imprisonment with release only after thirty years of actual sentence; no remission before that period
